physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the tailbone, the small knot of bone at the base of the spine, the floor of the body. It is the lowest point, the part that touches the chair, the ground, the earth. The whole long column above it stacks down to this one place. It is fitting that the code of the long climb begins in the part of the body that sits closest to the dirt.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. Greed is felt low. A tightness around the base, a clenched seat, an animal pressure that does not let the body rest. The hunger to climb shows up first in the body as a refusal to settle. Sleep gets short. The breath rides high in the chest and never reaches down. The base stays locked because some old part is sure that to relax the grip is to fall behind.

The climb out is also bodily, and slower than the mind wants. It begins with weight going down. The seat softens. The breath finds the floor of the belly. The base unlocks one small notch at a time, and the energy that used to grasp outward starts to move upward through the spine on its own. The traditions call this the serpent uncoiling. It is not a metaphor laid on top of the body. It is the body doing what the body does when it stops being hurried.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the bone, this code answers to a single amino acid, Serine. Serine is one of the amino acids the body can make for itself, built quietly out of what is already inside. It sits at a busy crossroads in the cell's chemistry, a hub other compounds branch off from, a giver of pieces to molecules further down the line. Its name comes from the Latin for fluid, the watery part of blood.

There is a teaching in that. The code that looks like crude appetite, the engine of the climb, runs on a chemistry that is quietly self-made and quietly liquid. Not a fuel stockpiled and held. A fuel that moves. Serine helps build the soft walls of the cell, the part that decides what passes in and what passes out. The body is already practising, at the smallest scale, what the card is asking of the whole life. Keep the substance liquid. Let it flow where it is needed. The climb runs all the way down to this.
